research_question: What is the effect of phenobarbital compared with levetiracetam, each used as first-line anti-seizure medication, on all-cause mortality before hospital discharge in neonates with seizures?
outcome_description: All-cause mortality prior to hospital discharge (number of neonates who died from any cause between randomisation and initial hospital/NICU discharge out of the total randomised or analysed in each arm)
positive_direction: Higher risk of all-cause mortality before discharge with phenobarbital compared to levetiracetam (RR > 1 indicates higher mortality with phenobarbital, favouring levetiracetam)
search_queries: phenobarbital levetiracetam neonatal seizures randomized trial
phenobarbitone levetiracetam newborn seizures mortality trial
levetiracetam vs phenobarbital neonates controlled comparison
inclusion_criteria: Randomised or quasi-randomised controlled trials involving neonates (up to 28 days of age, term or preterm) with clinically or electrographically diagnosed seizures
Direct comparison of phenobarbital (or phenobarbitone) versus levetiracetam as first-line anti-seizure monotherapy
Reporting of all-cause mortality prior to hospital discharge or initial NICU discharge for the randomised/analysed groups
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic reviews, meta-analyses, narrative reviews, editorials, comments, or study protocols without results)

Studies not evaluating phenobarbital versus levetiracetam as first-line anti-seizure medication (e.g. seizure prophylaxis, second-line or add-on therapy after failure of a prior drug, or non-comparative cohorts)
No quantitative outcome data reported on all-cause mortality before hospital/NICU discharge (studies omitting mortality reporting entirely are excluded rather than imputed as zero)
Non-neonatal populations (older infants or pediatric patients) or completely unrelated clinical topics
moderators_to_extract: Seizure diagnosis method (electrographic/aEEG vs clinical diagnosis)
Study risk of bias / trial quality
effect_size_note: Risk Ratio (RR) calculated as the risk of mortality in the phenobarbital arm divided by the risk in the levetiracetam arm. RR > 1 indicates higher mortality with phenobarbital (favours levetiracetam). Analyses follow intention-to-treat principles based on the original randomized arm, including in crossover or add-on settings. Studies with zero events in an arm are retained with zero events.
